techniques.title: Turn a rough mass into deliberate clusters
techniques.when: A silhouette reads at a distance but looks accidental on its native grid.
decisions: Separate silhouette edges, overlap edges, and light boundaries. Each needs a different contour.
Choose a short staircase rhythm for each straight segment. Let curved segments change run length gradually.
Reserve deliberate interruptions for joints, chips, leaves, or identity cues.
pixel_actions: Inspect the suspect rectangle with pixel_lab. Follow the boundary in row order.
Remove a double-width elbow or relocate one step where a line changes slope by accident.
Break a highlight that follows every outline step; join it to the plane it describes.
Merge unrelated flecks into a larger shape or remove them. Keep isolated eyes and glints when they carry the read.
techniques.check: The contour remains clear at 1x and the enlarged edge describes the same surface.
techniques.failure: Cleaning every irregularity produces a sterile outline or removes the identity cue.
techniques.exercise: Repair one awkward contour with the same grid and palette. State which coordinates change and what they clarify.

techniques.title: Design reusable color roles
techniques.when: Extra colors do not improve the separation of forms.
decisions: Assign colors to visible jobs before tuning individual hex values.
Share a shadow or highlight across materials when the lighting supports it.
Choose hue shifts from the light and environment. Straight ramps remain valid when the brief calls for them.
pixel_actions: Build a dark/base/light trial on the actual object, not just a palette strip.
Merge two colors occupying the same value job, then inspect the lost boundaries.
Spend a separate accent on the focal cue only after the object reads without it.
techniques.check: At native size the intended planes separate in grayscale and color; the accent has a useful location.
techniques.failure: A pleasing swatch arrangement becomes muddy when adjacent clusters use neighboring colors.
techniques.exercise: Render one form with two different value allocations while keeping its silhouette fixed.

techniques.title: Construct light from surface orientation
techniques.when: The sprite looks inflated, flat, or lit from incompatible directions.
decisions: Name the primary source, visible planes, and where one mass occludes another.
Use only the value groups the grid can distinguish. Two values can suffice; three are a useful experiment, not a minimum.
Additional lights need a declared role and must not erase the main form.
pixel_actions: Fill whole planes before adding specular marks.
Move a central highlight onto the surface facing the light.
Add a narrow contact shadow where two masses overlap; avoid outlining every plane equally.
techniques.check: Without texture, a viewer can infer the main volume and light direction.
techniques.failure: Uniform dark rims explain the outline but contradict the surface.
techniques.exercise: Relight one unchanged silhouette from the opposite side. Rebuild plane clusters, not just the palette.

techniques.title: Use a measured scaffold for volume
techniques.when: Roof, wall, wheel, or limb depths disagree.
decisions: Choose the screen-space axes and a scale unit. A two-across/one-up diagonal is a useful pixel dimetric convention, not every form's contour.
Map hidden box edges in the construction sketch so visible corners agree.
Separate structural symmetry from the asymmetry of lighting.
pixel_actions: Place anchor points and construct visible faces from their shared corners.
Check parallel segments against the chosen step pattern.
Replace scaffolds with authored bevels and contours after the volume agrees.
Mirror unlit geometry if appropriate, then relight it; do not blindly mirror the finished highlight.
techniques.check: The object occupies a coherent volume when its decorative details are hidden.
techniques.failure: Forcing every organic edge onto the construction axes destroys its shape.
techniques.exercise: Build a small stepped block with a cutout and one overhang before constructing an isometric machine.

techniques.title: Build foliage from lit overlapping masses
techniques.when: A canopy is a green blob or a field of unrelated bright pixels.
decisions: Choose species through crown shape, trunk gesture, and branch spacing.
Create a small leaf-bundle motif whose contour is useful even without its texture.
Use related dark/base/light mappings to place bundle depth.
pixel_actions: Place rear bundles, trunk, and front bundles in an explicit overlap order.
Put leaf-shaped marks where the crown turns into light; keep broad quiet areas.
Repair tiny holes and accidental peaks created where motifs overlap.
For conifers, construct branch tiers around a trunk guide instead of reusing a round deciduous bundle.
techniques.check: Crown volume survives flat values, and the species cue survives removal of leaf detail.
techniques.failure: A distinctive speck repeated in every bundle reveals the stamp.
techniques.exercise: Make two trees from the same original motif vocabulary with different crown silhouettes.

techniques.title: Make rock structure carry the material
techniques.when: Stone looks like a speckled ball or a metal gem.
decisions: Choose fracture behavior: broad sedimentary bands, angular breaks, or rounded weathering.
Allocate a few unequal facets instead of many equal triangles.
Let cliff strata and object rocks share a geological vocabulary.
pixel_actions: Cut the silhouette with one dominant face and an offset secondary ledge.
Shade the top and side as connected regions.
Put one fracture across a face; taper or stop it before every edge becomes outlined.
techniques.check: Facets explain volume in grayscale while fractures remain subordinate.
techniques.failure: Uniform glints and perfectly repeated diagonals turn rough stone into polished crystal.
techniques.exercise: Use one palette to make a rounded boulder and a split slab with visibly different structures.

techniques.title: Build connected flow and reflection shapes
techniques.when: Water becomes scattered white dashes or blue terrain.
decisions: Choose surface direction, shoreline, and whether the view shows reflection or submerged objects.
Separate waterfall lip, falling sheet, and splash if all are visible.
Use the flow direction to organize highlights.
pixel_actions: Draw connected dark and light surface masses first.
Break a few bands into subordinate fragments without losing their common direction.
Compress reflected shapes along the surface and interrupt them where ripples cross.
Keep shoreline foam distinct from specular highlights in open water.
techniques.check: Flow and surface orientation read without animation.
techniques.failure: Every region has the same streak density, so neither depth nor focus survives.
techniques.exercise: Create one still wave crest and one calm shoreline using different cluster rhythms.

techniques.title: Design masonry around its structural cadence
techniques.when: Brick detail overwhelms the wall or creates a visible grid in repeats.
decisions: Choose a brick-and-grout period that fits the tile extent when seamless repetition is required.
Separate top faces, wall faces, and recesses by their spatial role.
Treat damage as a variation layer, not the defining base pattern.
pixel_actions: Lay out joints as a temporary construction guide.
Fill the structural blocks, then suppress joints that compete with the whole wall.
Add selected chipped corners or value shifts; leave some runs uninterrupted.
Inspect the center junction of a 3x3 repeat and around the doorway.
techniques.check: The wall remains a large form; individual bricks become secondary information.
techniques.failure: A high-contrast grout lattice appears more strongly than the building.
techniques.exercise: Author a plain wall tile and one damaged variant with matching edge behavior.

techniques.title: Separate metal, glass, and matte surfaces by edge behavior
techniques.when: Several materials differ only in hue.
decisions: Choose where a hard reflection crosses a plane and where the surface stays quiet.
Distinguish a transparent window boundary from an opaque armor seam.
Use a broader light region for matte surfaces than for a hard specular edge.
pixel_actions: Bevel a structural corner before adding a glint.
Place a compact high-contrast reflection and preserve an adjacent dark region.
For glass, retain the rim and one selective interior cue instead of filling the whole object with shine.
techniques.check: The intended materials differ in grayscale at the target resolution.
techniques.failure: Bright dots on every corner make all surfaces glitter and erase the focal cue.
techniques.exercise: Render the same simple container as metal and glass without changing its hue family.

techniques.title: Use a posed dummy to control anatomy
techniques.when: Equipment hides a weak pose, or limbs attach in implausible places.
decisions: Choose proportion from the character and runtime grid, not a universal head count.
Place the support point, pelvis, rib cage, head, and limb endpoints before costume.
Reserve negative gaps that separate the action's important limbs or equipment.
pixel_actions: Use a few temporary colors to separate body parts.
Shift the torso and pelvis until the support and line of action agree.
Give the nearest limb a useful overlap; omit a far detail if it muddies the pose.
Fit armor, fur, or clothing around the dummy instead of replacing its anatomy.
techniques.check: The pose and weight read as a silhouette before facial or costume details.
techniques.failure: Symmetric limbs erase a turning gesture, or equipment floats away from the grip.
techniques.exercise: Construct a braced and a relaxed pose on the same grid with the same body proportions.

techniques.title: Allocate face cues and hair as separate masses
techniques.when: A face reads only when enlarged or hair dissolves into strands.
decisions: Reserve room for the expression cue before decorating the hair.
Choose a skull mass, facial plane, and hairline that explain the head angle.
Keep the most recognizable hair break in the outer contour.
pixel_actions: Place eye/brow relationships as a compact group.
Join locks into a few masses that follow the head, then add selective breaks.
Delete a mouth or nose pixel if it changes the intended expression incorrectly.
techniques.check: Facing and expression survive the native read without a title.
techniques.failure: Every feature is individually present but their spacing implies a different face.
techniques.exercise: Change one expression using only a small face region while protecting the head contour.

techniques.title: Spend tiny grids on distinctive relationships
techniques.when: A small asset is a miniature of a large drawing instead of a readable symbol.
decisions: Rank subject, facing, action, and identity cues. Declare which information is intentionally omitted.
Reserve cells for one separating gap and one identity cue before surface detail.
Redesign each requested size around the relationships it can retain.
pixel_actions: Widen a head, tool, cockpit, or handle if its relationship defines the subject.
Remove sampled micro-detail and merge neighboring surface regions.
Move a single cue by one cell and compare at native size; a tiny change can alter the whole read.
techniques.check: The strongest plausible blind interpretation matches the brief.
techniques.failure: All requested details exist as isolated pixels, but the object is not recognizable.
techniques.exercise: Author an 8x8 and a 16x16 version independently; state the information removed from the smaller master.

techniques.title: Make an item identifiable among its neighbors
techniques.when: A polished item looks generic or is confused with another item in the set.
decisions: Define the action or resource the item represents.
Choose a mass relationship, cutout, or protrusion that distinguishes it from its nearest competitor.
Fix family padding, baseline, light, and outline policy before authoring variations.
pixel_actions: Block the main mass and its distinguishing attachment.
Place material shading inside that construction.
Test on the actual interface background next to the most similar item.
Remove a decorative mark if it competes with the affordance.
techniques.check: The family looks related, but each item can be identified without its color or label.
techniques.failure: Palette swaps are doing the work of different silhouettes.
techniques.exercise: Make a key, tool, and consumable that share light and palette roles but have distinct outlines.

techniques.title: Build a usable neighborhood before expanding a tileset
techniques.when: One tile looks good but repeats, corners, or terrain transitions fail.
decisions: Separate a neutral base, transitions, and optional landmarks.
Choose whether shadows and vegetation are baked or overlaid from the runtime contract.
Build only the connection cases the requested neighborhood needs.
pixel_actions: Author the base and inspect a 3x3 repeat before adding variants.
Construct edge, outer corner, and inner corner masters on that base.
Assemble an actual concave and convex patch; inspect its central junctions.
Break conspicuous stripes and landmarks while retaining the edge contract.
techniques.check: The surface reads continuously in a repeated and mixed neighborhood.
techniques.failure: Opposite edge colors match, but a diagonal or repeated landmark remains obvious.
techniques.exercise: Use a base and a few transitions to assemble one small terrain patch with an inner corner.

techniques.title: Allocate contrast across depth bands
techniques.when: A background is busy or its planes collapse into one layer.
decisions: Choose the focal subject and the quiet area around it.
Map sky, distance, middle ground, and foreground as value bands adapted to the scene.
Define how contrast, cluster size, and color shift with distance; fog and emissive scenes may change the default.
pixel_actions: Draw large overlapping masses before texture.
Use fewer internal boundaries in distant planes.
Build clouds from overlapping lobes whose lit edges share a direction.
Place the foreground subject in the scene before spending detail on the background.
techniques.check: Depth and focus remain visible in grayscale and at the intended display size.
techniques.failure: Every plane uses the same dark outline and the same texture scale.
techniques.exercise: Create a valley and a forest using the same palette roles but different depth spacing.

techniques.title: Build architecture from linked volumes
techniques.when: A building is a decorated rectangle with no convincing structure.
decisions: Pick a recognizable roof, tower, entrance, or industrial mass as the main identity cue.
Use the doorway or tile foundation as the scale unit.
Plan front/back relationships and overhangs before windows.
pixel_actions: Place the dominant roof or tower, then connect its supporting wall planes.
Align additions to the same construction axes.
Use eave and doorway shadows to explain recesses.
Add window rhythm only where it supports scale; leave large wall regions quiet.
techniques.check: The building remains coherent when windows and wall texture are hidden.
techniques.failure: Every surface has equal detail, but walls do not meet the roof.
techniques.exercise: Make two structures with different functions using one shared scale and construction convention.

techniques.title: Encode machine function in the silhouette
techniques.when: A ship or robot has many panels but no convincing function or weight.
decisions: Choose propulsion, payload, controls, and support modules.
Express speed, armor, or reach through unequal mass allocation.
For mechs, set the torso, hip support, and feet before extremities; a mechanical torso need not imitate a human chest.
pixel_actions: Block the functional modules and one cutout or spacing cue.
Establish facing with cockpit placement, taper, or leg overlap.
Attach weapons and engines structurally, then bevel large faces.
Reserve a few optics or vents as accents; remove decorative panel grids.
techniques.check: Function, orientation, and weight remain plausible in flat silhouette.
techniques.failure: A symmetric badge replaces a directional craft, or heavy equipment has no support.
techniques.exercise: Make fast and heavy variants at one resolution by changing their mass allocation, not their palette.

techniques.title: Use motion references to construct a readable frame master
techniques.when: The asset will animate, or a reference GIF contains useful construction stages.
decisions: Classify the reference as a process recording, an animation loop, or a changing presentation.
For a process, compare structure, planes, and finish. For motion, inspect actual key poses and contact points.
Keep the frame's action phase, equipment ownership, and contact pivot explicit.
pixel_actions: Sample a few frames to locate useful sections, then inspect chosen originals.
Build a posed dummy before the costume or equipment.
Preserve identity masses and action gaps when detailing the frame.
Hand exact frame masters, durations, order, and pivots to spritesheet-expert when animation is requested.
techniques.check: A still frame reads on its own; motion claims require playback and timing review elsewhere.
techniques.failure: A contact sheet is mistaken for full animation proof, or a mirrored frame changes the equipped hand.
techniques.exercise: Extract evidence from a process GIF and translate one observed construction decision into an original still master.
